m7-t1.question: Why might workshop attendance and retention be associated without a causal workshop effect?
options: All participants are randomly selected automatically
m7-t1.explanation: A shared cause can explain the association.

m7-t1.question: What is reverse causality in this example?
options: The workshop definitely causes every exit
The data file is sorted backwards
A formula has a negative sign
Intention to stay may influence workshop attendance
m7-t1.explanation: The direction of influence may differ from the proposed story.

m7-t1.question: What is the illustrative difference-in-differences estimate for changes −8 and −2 points?
What is needed beyond the arithmetic for a causal interpretation?
m7-t1.explanation: The estimate depends on assumptions such as comparable trends.

m7-t1.question: When should evaluation outcomes be defined?
options: Only after finding a favourable metric

m7-t2.question: What is precision for four true exits among eight flagged records?
What is recall for four detected exits out of ten actual exits?
Why is a 90% accuracy claim insufficient in this example?
m7-t2.explanation: Class imbalance can make a trivial classifier look strong.

m7-t2.question: Which is an example of leakage when predicting future exits?
options: Holding out a later test period
Using an exit-processing date already known only after exit
Using a pre-period authorised aggregate workload measure
m7-t2.explanation: Post-outcome information creates unrealistically optimistic evaluation.

m7-t2.question: What does the classroom model review authorise?
options: Unrestricted use of real HR records
Learning from synthetic aggregate examples only
m7-t2.explanation: Real deployment requires separate governance and is outside the course exercise.

m7-t3.question: What is Group B’s selection rate for 12 of 40?
What is the B/A rate ratio for 30% and 40%?
What does that ratio alone establish?
options: A mandate to reject more candidates
A disparity signal requiring context and investigation
m7-t3.explanation: A screening ratio does not identify cause or legal status.

m7-t3.question: How should real demographic attributes be obtained for analysis?
options: Only through authorised lawful processes, not inference from names
m7-t3.explanation: Sensitive-data handling needs purpose, authority and safeguards.

m7-t3.question: What is part of responsible intervention governance?
options: Human accountability and a route to correct data or contest decisions
m7-t3.explanation: Consequential use requires broader safeguards than a technical metric.

questions.question: Workshop participants have lower exits, but participation is voluntary. What threatens a causal claim?
options: Selection differences such as motivation or manager support
questions.explanation: A shared cause can influence participation and retention.

questions.question: Pilot exit rate falls from 18% to 10%; comparison falls from 12% to 9%. What is the illustrative difference-in-differences estimate?
questions.explanation: Pilot change −8 minus comparison change −3 equals −5 points.

questions.question: What is needed before treating that estimate as causal?
options: Credible comparison assumptions, including underlying trends
questions.explanation: The arithmetic alone cannot validate the design.

questions.question: A sample has 90 stayers and 10 exits. A model predicts everyone stays. What are accuracy and exit recall?
questions.explanation: The model gets stayers right but detects no exits.

questions.question: A model flags 12 records, 6 of which exit; there are 15 actual exits. What are precision and recall?
A future-exit model includes completed exit-interview dates. What is the main defect?
options: Outcome leakage from information unavailable at prediction time
questions.explanation: Post-event data can make evaluation unrealistically strong.

questions.question: Group A selects 18 of 60 and B selects 8 of 40. What is B/A selection-rate ratio?
A selection-rate ratio is below a chosen screening threshold. What is justified?
options: Authorised investigation of disparity with context
A complete legal finding from the ratio alone
questions.explanation: A heuristic flags questions; it does not replace legal or substantive review.

questions.question: An analyst proposes inferring demographic groups from names to audit hiring. What should happen?
options: Do not infer; seek an authorised lawful data approach
questions.explanation: Sensitive attributes should not be guessed from proxies.

questions.question: A vendor model has high accuracy but no correction or contest route. What is missing?
options: Governance for consequential use, including human accountability
questions.explanation: Technical performance is not sufficient for responsible use.
